patent_grounding.rationale: Core train, paired gears, common carrier, alternative rotary exchange, carrier regulation and actuator alternatives align with claim passages read. Actuator description carefully treats bidirectionality as patent-disclosed alternatives rather than a simultaneously selected implementation. External boundary abstraction is identified as model scope, not asserted patent-specific prime mover.

functional_completeness.rationale: As an explicitly scoped claim-1 base model it captures the key components, paired-gear/shaft construction and carrier regulation. Optional energy recovery, coupling gear variants and dependent-claim extensions are reasonably excluded and explicitly noted.

flow_consistency.rationale: Interfaces use registered mechanical_rotary flows and compatible inout ports; every endpoint resolves. Carrier-to-train and carrier-to-actuator relations and the operating-shaft/external exchange are represented without cross-domain connections.

claim_traceability.rationale: The prior contradictory warning is removed. Remaining warning accurately says the operating-shaft/external and carrier interfaces are shown while internal gear-meshing topology is not mapped. Citations are present for model meta, all SJS ID-bearing records including ports, parts, flows, interfaces and action/step.

interfaces.rationale: The external rotary source/sink is separately named, not generic EXTERNAL; shaft boundary and internal carrier interfaces are distinct, compatible and recorded once. Abstract boundary and non-exhaustive alternative paths are disclosed in assumptions/warning.

textbook_application.rationale: The model distinguishes boundary interactions from internal subsystem interactions and represents typed compatible energy interfaces. Textbook guidance is applied only to modeling approach, not used as evidence for patent facts.

summary: Independently reviewed revision 4 SJS and supporting cited patent passages. Prior operating-shaft warning contradiction is resolved: remaining wording accurately acknowledges the modeled shaft/external interface and limits omission to detailed internal gear-meshing topology. Core claim-1 architecture and behavior are grounded; interface references and flow typing are consistent; model scope and optional alternatives are appropriately qualified. No unresolved findings.
